definition: The machinery behind text-to-video: spatiotemporal DiT blocks, temporal attention for motion consistency, and long-clip strategies like autoregressive chunking with overlap.
details: The machinery behind text-to-video: spatiotemporal DiT blocks, temporal attention for motion consistency, and long-clip strategies like autoregressive chunking with overlap. Object permanence and physics remain the visible failure modes, fueling the world-model debate (see World Models).

explainer.lead: Video Generation Internals covers the machinery behind text-to-video: spatiotemporal DiT blocks, temporal attention for motion consistency, and long-clip strategies like autoregressive chunking with overlap. It matters because object permanence and physics remain the visible failure modes, fueling the world-model debate.

tiers.eli5: The system builds a video in pieces and blends the seams, but it still sometimes loses track of objects or breaks the laws of physics.
tiers.practitioner: Builders combine spatiotemporal DiT blocks with temporal attention and generate long clips via autoregressive chunking with overlap. The known pitfall is that object permanence and physics still fail visibly.
tiers.paperLevel: Described by three mechanisms — spatiotemporal DiT blocks, temporal attention for motion consistency, and autoregressive chunking with overlap for long clips — with object permanence and physics as the visible failure modes. No formulas or quantitative limits are given.

explainer.example: To make a long clip, the model generates chunks autoregressively with overlap so the pieces join, while temporal attention keeps motion consistent across them.
